_comment: CALIBRATION GATE for the GPU proxy against real chip-C Trainium pairs (research/sim-data/validation-pairs.json). Every run is train.py (K60 = recipes/K60/train.py) on CUDA with a VIRTUAL charged clock (--clock virtual --step-seconds k1,k2,k4) so accum phases, MTP stages, cooldown and EMA levels switch at the Trainium step numbers, and --steps 2314 for every pair run: MODE (a), one shared K60 triple rescaled to the K57/lk35-era chip-C control count (see _steps_policy). Gate 2 (absolute level) is measured by the two _absolute_level runs at the Trainium reference step counts 2357 / 2361, outside `pairs`. The proxy is accepted by calibrate.py only if sign agreement >= 80% on the decisive pairs and the scale a of delta_trn ~ a*delta_gpu is bounded.

k60.what: K60 base exactly (train.py bakes LK 0.35 fnm, FF_ATTN_SRC=5:6,7,8, KO 0.3, ACC_IN_GRAPH 1, ramp3, QK 1.44, MOM_PEAK 0.95, WD_SCHED 0, softcap 15 / A 0, warmup 20, EMB_LR 0.30)

repeat.what: k60 seed 73 re-run on the SAME GPU: kernel nondeterminism null

repeat2.what: k60 seed 73 re-run on a DIFFERENT GPU: device/driver null (collapses to gpu 0 on a 1-GPU box)

relu2.what: K57-style relu^2 activation (the pair's control knobs)

rf.what: relu^2 with the custom backward (RF); FF_LEAKY_RELU2=0 added because K60 bakes 0.35 and the Trainium rf arm ran on the LEAKY=0 base

as0.what: attention-source reuse OFF (empty FF_ATTN_SRC disables; the pair's control knob)

noramp.what: no k1 phase (the ramp3 pair's control)

abs_base.what: gate 2 only: same env as as0 (K59 lineage) at 2357 steps; separate arm name so calibrate.py's arm-keyed statistics ignore it

abs_asa.what: gate 2 only: same env as k60 (K60 as scored) at 2361 steps; separate arm name so it stays out of the k60 base seed spread

_env_rule: run env = defaults.env + run.env on top of the K60 file's baked defaults; each arm carries the pair's own treatment or control knob set, plus any K60-baked knob the pair's base did not have reset to that base's value (rf adds FF_LEAKY_RELU2=0). Both arms of every pair therefore share the K60 base (LK 0.35 + attention-source reuse), which is a base shift relative to the K57/g5/g4-era Trainium measurements and is part of what the calibration measures.
_steps_policy: MODE (a), NOT the mode (b) log replay that PROTOCOL.md 3.2 describes: fleet.py build_command emits one '--clock virtual --step-seconds k1=0.2950,k2=0.5060,k4=0.9280 --steps 2314' (fleet.DEFAULT_STEP_SECONDS = K60-lineage chip-C medians) for every pair run, and train_gpu.py rescales that triple by one factor (1.02587) so the clock-driven run ends at 2314 = the K57/lk35-era chip-C control step count (s73 2314, s58 2310, s67 2313; lk35 2326). The rescaled walk switches at accum phase 2 step 329, phase 3 step 813, EMA level 19 step 1190, MTP 270/467/640/813/931/1048/1166/1284: 3-9 steps EARLIER than the chip-C LK35 controls (0816_R_g7lk35_s73 / 0913_R_g7lk35_s58 train.log: 333/332, 820/818, 1198/1197, MTP 274/472/646/820/939/1057/1175/1293). No run replays a Trainium log (make_train_gpu.py --step-seconds-from-log / --stop-step are not used by fleet.py; a per-pair mode (b) needs fleet.py changes and is a later stage). Both arms of every pair share this schedule, so the GPU deltas are equal-step, equal-switch deltas. One shared base arm per seed keeps the fleet at ~39 runs. The g5/g4-era (2300/2150) and chip-D (2153) pairs are compared as deltas, which are step-count-insensitive to first order; their Trainium targets are corrected to equal steps by calibrate.py (delta_eq = delta_raw + 0.057 ln(T/C)). configs/prescreen.json (300 steps) is a SMOKE TEST of the clock and data path, not the PROTOCOL 5 pre-screen (which is four runs at the K60 schedule, 2361 steps); memory: a 120-300-step screen predicts early loss only.

_absolute_level.what: PROTOCOL.md 3.3 gate 2 (absolute level; a smoke test, PROTOCOL 4 row 12): two runs at the Trainium reference step counts, deliberately OUTSIDE `pairs` and under their own arm names: calibrate.py matches pair runs on (seed, steps) and keys the base seed spread / nulls on arm k60 / repeat*, so abs_base (2357) and abs_asa (2361) enter no delta, no null and no seed spread.

abs_base_s73.target_run: C40_cold_K59 (chip C, seed 73, 2357 steps, TT 1793; validation-pairs.json reh_k59_vs_k57t treatment) = K59 lineage = K60 with attention-source reuse off

abs_asa_s73.target_run: C41_cold_K60 (chip C, seed 73, 2361 steps, TT 1793; rehearsal of the official 0.9655) = K60 as scored

_absolute_level.note: --steps 2357 / 2361 rescale the same shared triple by their own factor, so these two runs also switch at the rescaled K60 walk, not at the C40/C41 logs. Beyond 0.03 = structural: check --data-world 8, --eval-emulate-ranks 8, FF_LAMBDA_0D=1 (PROTOCOL 3.3). They are not paired with each other: different step counts, and the asa delta is measured by the asa pair at 2314.

_decisive: calibrate.py decides: |delta_eq| >= 0.0005 with a stable sign over k in [0.045, 0.070]. Expected decisive: lk35_vs_relu2, lk35_vs_rf, lk35_vs_lk05, asa, asb, mp97, ramp3, r3p30 (8); null-expected at equal steps: rf_vs_relu2, wd_sched1, softcap165, emb_lr036, qk16; ambiguous: ko03, mp93, warmup40. Report sign agreement per family too: the two accum_sched pairs test the equal-step correction, not a model change.

_dropped.acc_in_graph: REMOVED 29 Sep (pair k60 vs acc0, runs acc0_s53 / acc0_s67): defaults.args carries --compile none, and train_gpu.py _gpu_normalise_args (make_train_gpu.py:297-303) forces FF_ACC_IN_GRAPH=0 in eager mode (recorded as acc_in_graph_disabled), so both arms ran the same eager accumulation path and the pair was a guaranteed tie that would have entered sign_agreement_all for $5-8. PROTOCOL 3.1: FF_ACC_IN_GRAPH is a Neuron graph-capture flag with no GPU pair; testing it needs --compile inductor and a separate context (PROTOCOL 4 row 7). The Trainium refs acc_in_graph_s53/s67/s58 stay in validation-pairs.json.

_seeds: the pair's own Trainium seed(s) where they exist (73/58/67/53) so per-seed sign rows are possible; a second seed everywhere.
_nulls: k60_s73_repeat (same GPU as k60_s73) and k60_s73_repeat2 (other GPU) measure kernel / device nondeterminism.
